title: Aldi Supermarkets - General Discussion
body:
O.P.
this post was edited
Please use this thread for general discussion of Aldi stores, including (but not limited to):
in-store experiences
customer service
facilities (e.g. baskets, trolleys, aisles, car parks)
For discussion regarding specific Aldi food and grocery products , please use this thread .
For discussion regarding Aldi gadgets , please use this thread .
For Aldi Mobile , please use this thread .
If you think a particular Aldi product (i.e. TV or other home theatre product or Aldi white goods ) can sustain a discussion of its own, please create a thread in the relevant forum.
If you are unsure about any of the above, please start a thread in TWAM and ask for a mod's opinion/direction.

---- replies ----
[User #734891423 postsphixxyGoose noisesWhirlpool Enthusiast] Let me kick this off here because if now mentioned in the other Aldi threads we'll get put in the naughty corner! This is for the benefit of all those that whinge about Aldi's model, no baskets, paying for trolleys, small counters, etc, etc!
Because their model is based on getting you the cheapest prices possible while still making money and for that privilege I'll accept every price cutting measure they need. Why can't so many others, who instead prefer to complain about it!? People like Dick Smith whine about them taking business from Coleworths and the rest and squeezing their profit margins as if a bad thing but every dollar someone saves at Aldi gets pumped back into the Aussie economy in other ways. The thousand dollars I've saved over time at Aldi means I can now buy a well needed new sofa that otherwise just would not have happened. They are more than happy with their model and if customers can't or won't adjust they can always go back to the others and pay far more for an equal quality product.
I love Aldi for the speed not just for their own cost savings but for my own convenience. Fast in, fast out suits me as much as them! Last thing I want is the cashier starting with a forced by management "How has your day been", when you know damn well they are not his/her thoughts at all.
[User #9299919175 postsSentient BeingsWhirlpool Forums Addict] My local doesn't have baskets because the manager told me they get stolen.
No matter whether I'm planning on buying one item or ten, I always take a trolley. It's more convenient in the long run and better at the checkout especially for those behind you.
The plastic Woolworth's token fits Aldi and Coles trollies too. I keep a couple in my wallet. In Katoomba all the supermarket trollies use tokens now. Coles introduced the token system a few months ago whereas Woolies and Aldi have always had them.
[User #36866228492 postsulmoWhirlpool Forums Addict] I've never (well, not that I can remember) ever felt bothered by no baskets.
If I'm going in for a few things, I can carry them. If I'm going in for more than a few things, I'll take one or two Aldi bags from the boot. If it's a 'big' shop, I'll get a trolley. I have an Aldi trolley token key ring attachment, and I also have some loose coins in the car for car parking or similar things.
Every time I go into Aldi, I usually have a fair idea of the amount of goods I intend to buy. So I just prepare.
[User #22838266154 postsTýr of AesirLet me be your eyes, Blind OneWhirlpool Forums Addict] phixxy writes...
Fast in, fast out suits me as much as them!
Hear hear.
I have trolly bags, and just pack directly into those at the checkout. Aldi's range has improved over the years, and I've been happy with since I first went to Aldi over 20 years ago....pretty much when they first opened in SW Sydney.
Whinging about packing one's own bag is just laziness.
My local Aldi is the new style, and it looks good too now. As said the money saved is amazing. Just for fun, I've plugged in my normal shop into Colesworth pages, and I have saved at least $50/shop using Aldi for 90% of my groceries. I still visit Woolies for some items Aldi doesn't sell.
[User #55247622923 postspedrovyes, I changed it....Whirlpool Forums Addict] I think it is more than just "stopping theft" for having the tokens. If someone wants to steal a trolley, they won't be worried by the token. I think it has more to do with the fact they don't need to hire trolley staff to collect trolleys from all over the carpark (because folks are lazy and can't be bothered putting them back). It would appear the token is enough incentive for people to put the trolleys were they actually go. It wouldn't bother me doing it at any shop.
Personally I don't mind the token and no-basket approach of Aldi. I either buy enough to carry only, or get a trolley. Simple really.
[User #55247622923 postspedrovyes, I changed it....Whirlpool Forums Addict] Last year, while in Germany, I took great pleasure in walking around an Aldi store near my hotel. Just to see what is common, and what was different to our stores in Aus. The layout was similar to the older Aus layout. Not sure if/when they may do a refurb also. The bread roll/pretzel vending wall was awesome. About half the range was different to what we get here. It was very interesting.
[User #402839740 postsAussieSueJWhirlpool Enthusiast] If I am heading into Aldi for a couple of things, I usually just chuck stuff into my reusable bag which I bring with me so have never needed to use a basket. At the checkout, out it comes from the bags onto the conveyor belt and as it is being scanned, it goes straight back into the bag....hence i have never really missed the basket.
I have enjoyed Aldi as they have introduced a lot more options for healthy eating – a whole lot earlier than either Coles or Woolies. Aldi seems always seem to one step ahead of the game for some stuff as compared to Coles and Woolies.
[User #2248256347 postsnickyyboyyWhirlpool Forums Addict] I never thought about a basket until the other thread exploded about them. I just put them in my reusable bag, unload then fill back up on checkout. Baskets would just create more clutter as people are in different positions when finishing placing their items up on for checkout. I mean they just going to end up back in my bag anyway for a small purchase so don't really see a need for baskets.
[User #554392348 postsDottyWhirlpool Forums Addict] One of the many things we appreciate about Aldi is the lack of musak, or piped music. So much more peaceful, although the constant "we are closing checkout 4, please go to the next available checkout" is pretty intrusive. Would be good if that could be less loud
[User #7038035095 postsalmondy23Eat an almond nutWhirlpool Forums Addict] phixxy writes...
cheapest prices possible
Is it really? So many things there are not much cheaper than Coles at all. There are some things I buy, thinking of toilet paper, biscuits and the cheap cola as one example, but if you stock up on Coles specials, then the price difference is pretty negligible for the trouble you go for at Aldi. I was trained by my petulant t mother when I was a kid to always stock up on Woolies supermarket specials when they come on, which I still do.
I could readily provide a comparison for basic items I've bought recently (eggs, milk, bread, rice, pasta all spring to mind immediately). Not to mention that cc surcharge they whack on without telling you! woops...
https://www.choice.com.au/sh opping/everyday-shopping/sup ermarkets/articles/cheapest-groceries-australia
This article says that if you buy supermarket-brand stuff from Coles/Woolies, the price is only 10% dearer than the small basket of items from Aldi. So, where are these super-duper savings that people are funding their retirement with coming from?
People like Dick Smith whine about them taking business from Coleworths and the rest and squeezing their profit margins as if a bad thing but every dollar someone saves at Aldi gets pumped back into the Aussie economy in other ways.
Its true that Aldi sources a lot of stuff from Australia, but not everything; and any leftover profit is returned to Europe. Certainly worth a thought for the Aldi-obsessives, even if you ridicule that as whingeing.
Fast in, fast out
Can you explain clearly how their model of no baskets, having to insert $1 coins and being forced to use trolleys is "fast-in, fast-out"? Who really wants to spend a long time in supermarkets after work? No-one! And queues are always worse at Aldi with no self check-out and place to pack bags.
Ultimately, whatever, it is what it is and if you dont like it, dont shop there! Yes its true and thats why we dont. I do find it intrinsically fascinating how much Aldi obsessors defend it vigorously, as if it were their own family business and how valuable their model is and how much you should adapt to it to save cash (even though its easily proven you dont).
Its also strange how every cashier every time as you leave tells you 'you can find the Aldi catalogue on your way out over there'....usually stores show it on the way in before you buy stuff!!
[User #55247622923 postspedrovyes, I changed it....Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
almondy23 writes...
I was trained by my petulant t mother when I was a kid to always stock up on Woolies supermarket specials when they come on, which I still do.
Reminds me of the current Aldi ad :) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vzSLiM7hPIo
usually stores show it on the way in before you buy stuff!!
Normally the Aldi specials catalogue is advertising the upcoming special buys. Not so much the current ones. My local store has a big billboard as you walk in showing all the current special buys.
[User #2972181429 postswintersnowWhirlpool Enthusiast] almondy23 writes...
This article says that if you buy supermarket-brand stuff from Coles/Woolies, the price is only 10% dearer than the small basket of items from Aldi. So, where are these super-duper savings that people are funding their retirement with coming from?
They buy the brand name items full price and compare.
The only thing I buy full price from Coles or Woolworths is fruit and vegetables, meat (if reasonable), milk and their branded stuff.
Everything like cleaning products and junk food is on a repetitive cycle of 50% off every 5 or so weeks.
[User #734891423 postsphixxyGoose noisesWhirlpool Enthusiast] almondy23 writes...
Its also strange how every cashier every time as you leave tells you 'you can find the Aldi catalogue on your way out over there'....usually stores show it on the way in before you buy stuff!!
From Wednesday on it's the catalogue for special buys for the following Wednesday and Saturday. It's no good at all to you as you walk through the door! Why is it so hard? They don't follow Colseworths model!
[User #1577044136 postshasher22Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Never had a problem with Aldi
Had to exchange a few items, no problems. Their meat is fine, can't really tell the difference between woolies.
Their own brand chocolate is flapping amazing, better than cadbury. I gave some to my friends and they agreed as well! Even their lemonade which is like 89c is amazing too! I used to buy sprite or schweppes lemonade and I found the aldi brand so much better.
But I feel sorry for the staff members, they seem overworked and the amount of abuse they get from older people astounds me. Nearly everytime I go, there's always an older person complaining to a rep about X.
I was walking past shopping for chips and this, around 5'5 maybe shorter elderly person was abusing the heck out of this staff member for her lack of logic. There's prices above the items if its a top shelf item, she was complaining that she couldn't see the price where she was standing and stating stuff like: "this company is bad, this company should cater for people like me, if im grabbing the item... how would i know the price!?" The rep told her the price and she said: "thats not good enough wheres the price?". The rep kindly said: "if you step back a bit, its at the to.....", then she cut him off and said: "I SHOULDN'T HAVE TO STEP BACK TO SEE THE PRICE! RAAWWRRRRR" and she went on a massive rant.......
[User #7038035095 postsalmondy23Eat an almond nutWhirlpool Forums Addict] phixxy writes...
Why is it so hard?
Cos I'm too busy trying to pack my bags and pay the cc surcharge to care about catalogues at this point. Would be great to hear your response to the other points I made to your opening post.
hasher22 writes...
they seem overworked and the amount of abuse
That is a further disadvantage of the cheapo Aldi model, it's just inevitable annoyed customers will take it out on staff. Even myself, it's frustrating when they are flinging items nearly off the bench and all they say is 'you can find the Aldi catalogue over there'. Of course they will cop the flak from those who haven't embraced the Aldi ethos as enthusiastically as others here.
